# Blueprint

> Post a job for robots. A site films one job that repeats. Blueprint turns the video into a job packet: the site's description, the video without sound, a first look at which robots could fit, and a simulation of the site when it is ready. Blueprint shares the description, the video and the simulation with the deployment companies it approves, so they can say if they can do the job. A site's name, address and contact details go to a company only when the site asks for an introduction. Free for sites.

The job packet holds the site's own sentence for the job. Blueprint adds a first look at which robots could fit when there is enough detail, using published specifications and where the robots have been used. Blueprint uses video to build a simulation of the site when it can. The job can still go to companies while the simulation is being built.

Blueprint sends each job automatically to the deployment companies it has approved. The job packet gives the site's description and what counts as done when known. The packet includes the required video without sound and adds the simulation when it is ready. A company answers "Apply", "Not a fit" or "Need more details". Blueprint can't promise any will say yes. After a company applies, the site can ask for an introduction to each company it wants to meet. After an introduction the company gets the site's name, address and contact details, and the site gets the company's name and contact details. Any work is agreed between the site and the company. Nothing is charged today. A simulation is a bounded estimate and never certifies physical performance or safety.
